newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian leader says he committed to privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian leader says he committed to privatisation.

text.p: Nigeria's military ruler General Sani Abacha said on Wednesday that his government was committed to reducing the state's role in the economy and to encouraging foreign investment.
The administration wanted to encourage private ownership of industries and commercial ventures, he said when he received outgoing Pakistani ambassador, Mukarram Syed.
"The current policy direction is aimed at encouraging foreign investors into the Nigerian economy," an official statement quoted Abacha as saying.
Finance minister Anthony Ani said last month that Nigeria was seriously considering selling its oil joint ventures and privatising the oil refineries.
Nigeria, sub-Saharan Africa's biggest economy, has been in recession since 1993 when the country slid into crisis over annulment of an election that would have restored democracy.

Free market policies in place since early 1995 have stabilised the economy and analysts say the privatisation being mulled could be worth more than $50 billion and restore economic growth if well executed.
Last month Ani told a seminar in Lagos, "Privatisation will open our economy up for the foreign investment we very much need."

The sales being considered include the government's 57 percent equity share in joint ventures with foreign oil firms that produce Nigerian crude oil and four refineries capable of turning nearly half a million barrels of crude oil into refined products daily.
The government is also poised to privatise the National Electric Power Authority and Nigeria Telecommunications.
